subject.title: feat: expose native chat timing in OpenTelemetry

question: Should the Windows tray adopt this full 19-instrument native-chat telemetry catalog as a supported operator-facing contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but signal names, lifecycle boundaries, cardinality, and long-term compatibility are product and observability-contract choices that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve after collector proof
options.body: Accept the proposed catalog once redacted Aspire evidence confirms the documented hierarchy, attributes, metrics, and privacy behavior on the current head.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Request a smaller first release centered on turn, send, response-wait, and response-receive signals, deferring history and dropped-event telemetry until operational demand is demonstrated.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep native chat timing internal until the gateway and tray can share propagated trace context through a coordinated protocol design.

recommendation.title: Approve after collector proof
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed catalog once redacted Aspire evidence confirms the documented hierarchy, attributes, metrics, and privacy behavior on the current head.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available project-level routing candidate for native tray product and observability direction, although the file-level ownership trail is incomplete.
